In 1784 the Korean scholar Yi Seung-hun was baptised in Beijing and came home to baptise others. The Catholic Church in Korea is unusual in that it was started by Koreans themselves, before any foreign priest arrived.

Korean envoys had been bringing back Chinese books by Jesuits such as Matteo Ricci for over a century. A circle of young scholars of the Practical Learning school read them and grew interested in the faith. Yi Seung-hun joined an embassy to Beijing to learn more. Several members of the family of Jeong Yak-yong were among the early converts.

The Joseon state saw the faith as an attack on Confucian order, above all once converts refused ancestor rites. Waves of persecution followed in 1801, 1839, 1846 and 1866, and thousands were killed, including Yi Seung-hun himself. In 1984 the pope made 103 of the martyrs saints. Today Catholics are about a tenth of South Koreans, and Christianity as a whole is a major religion there.
